findings.title: CI Build Auto-Generates Weak Keystore When Signing Secrets Absent
findings.lower_trust_principal: Attacker with access to published APK
findings.result: Attacker can re-sign malicious updates with same identity, enabling persistent app replacement
findings.evidence: Lines 83-92 generate keystore with hardcoded 'android123' password when KEYSTORE_BASE64 secret unset. Keystore used to sign release APK.
findings.attack_scenario: If repository secrets are not configured, CI generates a self-signed keystore with well-known low-entropy password. Attacker extracts keystore from APK (standard Android tooling) and re-signs malicious updates. Users' devices accept updates signed with same key.
findings.remediation: 1. Remove fallback keystore generation; fail build if KEYSTORE_BASE64 secret absent. 2. Document release signing requirements. 3. Rotate any APKs published with auto-generated keystore.

findings.title: On-Device Password Hashing Uses Bare SHA-256 (No Key Stretching)
findings.result: Offline GPU cracking at ~10-50B attempts/sec; 8-char minimum falls in hours-days
findings.evidence: hashPassword() uses single SHA-256: Crypto.digestStringAsync(SHA256, `${salt}::${password}`). No PBKDF2, Argon2, scrypt, or iteration count. expo-crypto does not expose KDF.
findings.attack_scenario: Device lost/stolen. Attacker extracts AsyncStorage (rooted device, adb backup, forensic tool). Finds salt + SHA256(salt::password). With single fast hash, offline brute force recovers weak passwords quickly.
findings.remediation: Replace with PBKDF2 (expo-crypto + manual iterations, min 100k) or Argon2 (native module). Store iteration count in profile for future upgrades.

findings.title: Merge Deduplication by Case-Insensitive Fund Name Can Conflate Distinct Funds
findings.lower_trust_principal: N/A (data integrity violation during user-initiated merge)
findings.affected_resource: Portfolio analytics (XIRR, fee drag, CGT, fund-level breakdowns)
findings.result: Two funds differing only in case merged into one; entries combined, analytics corrupted
findings.evidence: fundKey = name.trim().toLowerCase(); fundsByName Map uses this key. No secondary discriminator (user_id, AMC code, ISIN). Case variance in user-entered fund names causes collision.
findings.attack_scenario: User has 'NMB Saral Bachat Fund-E' on phone and 'nmb saral bachat fund-e' in cloud (or another device). Merge treats as single fund. All entries combined under one fund_id. Dashboard XIRR, fee drag, CGT, monthly contributions all incorrect.
findings.remediation: Use composite key: (user_id, fund_name_lowercase). Since merge is per-user, add cloud user ID to key. Or add explicit fund-match confirmation step in merge UI.

findings.title: Deep Link Token Replay Possible If Web Backend Doesn't Enforce Single-Use
findings.attack_class: DESKTOP-MOBILE-AND-LOCAL-IPC.md#Deep-link, callback, and navigation attack classes / WEB-PROTOCOL-AND-AUTH.md#OAuth/OIDC request and callback binding
findings.trust_boundary: Google OAuth Callback (Deep Link) → Mobile App → Web Backend Token Exchange
findings.result: Replay of captured token yields valid session if web backend doesn't enforce single-use
findings.evidence: Client mints 16-byte nonce, sends to web /api/mobile/google. On callback, token from sahakarisip://auth/callback?token=... exchanged via /api/mobile/exchange. Client has no replay protection; relies entirely on server.
findings.attack_scenario: Attacker captures token (clipboard, notification preview, browser history). Replays to /api/mobile/exchange. If server doesn't mark token consumed, attacker obtains valid RLS JWT and accesses victim's portfolio.
findings.remediation: 1. Verify web backend marks nonce/token consumed on first exchange (idempotent rejection). 2. Add short expiry (≤5 min). 3. Consider binding token to device fingerprint at issuance.

findings.title: Android allowBackup="true" Exposes App Data via adb backup
findings.lower_trust_principal: Attacker with physical USB access to unlocked device
findings.affected_resource: AsyncStorage (local profiles, session, privacy settings), potentially SecureStore
findings.result: adb backup extracts app data including financial records and auth tokens
findings.evidence: <application android:allowBackup="true" ... android:fullBackupContent="@xml/secure_store_backup_rules">. Backup API enabled; referenced XML may not exclude all sensitive keys.
findings.attack_scenario: Attacker with unlocked device runs 'adb backup -f backup.ab com.samimrrza.sahakarisip'. Backup includes AsyncStorage keys (sahakarisip.v1.*) and potentially SecureStore data (biometric entries with Supabase JWTs).
findings.remediation: Set android:allowBackup="false" in AndroidManifest.xml, or define fullBackupContent XML to explicitly exclude sahakarisip.v1.* keys and SecureStore.

findings.title: CSV Import Accepts User-Supplied units Without Cross-Field Validation
findings.affected_resource: Data integrity (XIRR, fee drag, CGT, portfolio value)
findings.result: Inconsistent units stored; dashboard recomputes from stored values producing incorrect analytics
findings.evidence: units = parsed.data.units ?? Math.floor(effectiveCash / nav). If units provided in CSV, used directly without verifying units * nav ≈ amount - DP_CHARGE. csvRowSchema allows optional units but no cross-field refine.
findings.attack_scenario: User imports CSV with units=999999 for a small amount. Entry stored with bogus units. Dashboard calculations (totalUnits, currentValue, XIRR, fee drag) all incorrect. Self-impact only; no cross-user boundary.
findings.remediation: Add Zod .refine() on csvRowSchema: if units provided, verify units === Math.floor((amount - DP_CHARGE) / nav). Reject rows violating SEBON whole-unit rule.

findings.title: .env File with Production Credentials Exists in Working Directory
findings.lower_trust_principal: Anyone with repo access if committed
findings.affected_resource: Supabase project identifier and anon key
findings.result: If committed, requires key rotation and exposes project URL
findings.evidence: .env contains EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY for production project. .gitignore excludes .env but file persists in workspace.
findings.attack_scenario: Developer runs 'git add .' accidentally committing .env. Anon key is public-by-design (RLS constrained) but project URL exposure aids reconnaissance. Key rotation required if leaked.
findings.remediation: 1. Delete .env from workspace; use .env.local (also gitignored) for local overrides. 2. Add pre-commit hook rejecting .env. 3. Rotate anon key if ever committed (Supabase Dashboard → API → Regenerate).

findings.title: Google OAuth Handoff — Web Backend Single-Use Token Enforcement
findings.result: Unknown — depends on web backend implementation
findings.evidence: Client relies on web backend to enforce single-use of handoff token. Web backend (sahakari-sip NextAuth) not in this repository.
findings.blocker: Web backend token consumption logic not observable in this repository.
findings.validation_plan: Owner deploys test instance, captures handoff token, exchanges twice, verifies second request fails (400/409).

findings.title: Supabase RLS Policies Correctly Enforce Per-User Isolation
findings.lower_trust_principal: Authenticated cloud user attempting cross-user access
findings.affected_resource: All user data tables (fund_config, entries, nav_history, notification_preferences, notifications_log)
findings.result: Unknown — depends on deployed Supabase RLS policies
findings.evidence: All cloud queries filter by user_id from JWT (RLS). Source assumes RLS policies exist: auth.uid() = user_id. Not verifiable from this repo.
findings.blocker: Supabase RLS policies are deployed configuration, not in source.
findings.validation_plan: Owner checks Supabase Dashboard → Authentication → Policies. Tests with two dummy users: sign in as user A, attempt to read user B's rows via Supabase client with user A's JWT.

findings.title: Android fullBackupContent XML Actually Excludes Sensitive Keys
findings.evidence: Manifest references @xml/secure_store_backup_rules but file content not reviewed. If missing or permissive, allowBackup=true enables full backup.
findings.blocker: XML file content not accessible in current workspace view.
findings.validation_plan: Owner inspects secure_store_backup_rules.xml. If missing or permissive, set allowBackup="false".
